title: Advanced user queries in Microsoft Graph: filter, search, count and stale sign-ins
summary: Ready-to-run requests for listing users with $filter, $select, $orderby, $count and $search, plus the signInActivity query for inactive accounts.
body:
## What it does
These requests cover the user queries admins need daily: enabled member accounts sorted by name, a count, a name search, guest users, and accounts that have not signed in since a given date. Several of them are advanced queries and need the ConsistencyLevel header.

## Requests

Enabled members, sorted, with total count (advanced query because $orderby is combined with $filter):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=accountEnabled eq true and userType eq 'Member'&$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName,department,jobTitle,createdDateTime&$orderby=displayName&$count=true&$top=100
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Count only:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/$count
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Search by display name or mail:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$search="displayName:meyer" OR "mail:meyer"&$select=id,displayName,mail&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Guest users (userType is the simplest and most robust filter):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=userType eq 'Guest'&$select=id,displayName,mail,createdDateTime,externalUserState&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Alternative through the guest UPN suffix. endsWith is only supported as an advanced query, and the # must be encoded as %23:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=endsWith(userPrincipalName,'%23EXT%23@contoso.onmicrosoft.com')&$select=id,displayName,mail,createdDateTime&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Disabled accounts:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=accountEnabled eq false&$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Accounts without a sign-in since a date (needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2). Per the documentation, a filter on signInActivity cannot be combined with other filterable properties, and the page size is limited to 500 when signInActivity is selected or filtered:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=signInActivity/lastSignInDateTime le 2026-08-20T00:00:00Z&$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName,accountEnabled,signInActivity&$top=500
```

## Response shape
```json
{
  "@odata.context": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/$metadata#users(...)",
  "@odata.count": 1842,
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$skiptoken=[token]",
  "value": [ { "id": "[object-id]", "displayName": "Anna Meyer" } ]
}
```
Follow @odata.nextLink until it is absent. Do not use $skip: the documentation states that $skip is not supported on the users list.

## How to adapt
- More attributes: extend $select; only the default set is returned without it.
- Licensed users: $filter=assignedLicenses/any(u:u/skuId eq [sku-guid]) with $count=true and ConsistencyLevel: eventual (test it in Graph Explorer first).
- Users without any license: $filter=assignedLicenses/$count eq 0&$count=true with ConsistencyLevel: eventual.
- Export to a spreadsheet: pipe the value array into your tool of choice, or use the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK with the same filter.

## Required permissions
- Users list: delegated User.ReadBasic.All (limited properties), User.Read.All; application User.Read.All.
- signInActivity: additionally AuditLog.Read.All, and the signed-in admin needs a role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader or Global Reader for delegated access.
- Guest users have restricted directory access by default and usually cannot list other users. Always request the least privileged permission that returns the properties you need.

## Common mistakes
- Omitting ConsistencyLevel: eventual together with $count=true on advanced queries leads to a 400 error such as "Request_UnsupportedQuery".
- Not encoding # in guest UPNs.
- Expecting $top above 999 (or above 500 with signInActivity) to be honoured; you get capped pages.
- Combining signInActivity filter with other filters, which is not supported.
- Using $skip for paging instead of nextLink.

## Performance and throttling notes
Always use $select; it reduces payload and latency. Advanced queries rely on an eventually consistent index, so a user created seconds ago may not appear yet. Identity and access requests are throttled per tenant and app; on HTTP 429 wait for the Retry-After header value before retrying, and avoid parallelising more than a few paging loops.

title: Entra sign-in log queries with $filter: failed sign-ins, Conditional Access blocks and per-user checks
summary: Practical /auditLogs/signIns requests for time windows, failures by error code, Conditional Access failures and per-user investigations, with paging advice.
body:
## What it does
The sign-in log is the first stop for lockouts, MFA problems and suspicious access. These requests return the events you actually need instead of the whole log. Results come back newest first, so you rarely need $orderby.

## Requests

All sign-ins in a time window (always limit the time range to avoid timeouts):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z and createdDateTime le 2026-11-19T23:59:59Z&$top=500
```

Failed sign-ins for one user:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=userPrincipalName eq 'anna@contoso.example' and status/errorCode ne 0 and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z&$top=100
```

Invalid username or password (error code 50126) in the last day:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=status/errorCode eq 50126 and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=200
```

Sign-ins blocked or failed by Conditional Access:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=conditionalAccessStatus eq 'failure' and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=200
```

Sign-ins to a particular application by name:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=startsWith(appDisplayName,'Microsoft Teams') and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=100
```

Interactive sign-ins only:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=isInteractive eq true and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=200
```

## Useful fields in the response
userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ipAddress, clientAppUsed, createdDateTime, conditionalAccessStatus, status/errorCode, status/failureReason, deviceDetail/operatingSystem, location/countryOrRegion, riskLevelDuringSignIn. Common error codes: 50126 (bad credentials), 50053 (account locked), 50074 (MFA required), 53003 (blocked by Conditional Access), 50057 (account disabled).

Paging: each response contains @odata.nextLink while more data exists. Follow the complete link; it contains the skiptoken.

## How to adapt
- Replace the date placeholders with the window you need, always in UTC with a trailing Z.
- For a SIEM-style daily export, run the first request for the previous day at 01:00 UTC and store the page tokens only until the run finishes.
- Add $select=id,createdDateTime,userPrincipalName,appDisplayName,ipAddress,status to cut payload size. Be aware that appliedConditionalAccessPolicies is large; request it only when you need it.

## Required permissions
- Delegated and application: AuditLog.Read.All.
- Delegated access additionally requires a Microsoft Entra role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Operator, Security Administrator or Global Reader.
- The appliedConditionalAccessPolicies property is only included if the caller can also read Conditional Access data (for example the Policy.Read.ConditionalAccess application permission, or roles such as Conditional Access Administrator or Security Reader).

## Common mistakes
- Querying without a time filter: the call may time out because the log is large.
- Using local time instead of UTC in the filter.
- Expecting more history than your license provides; retention depends on the Microsoft Entra ID license (free tenants keep a short window; P1 and P2 keep longer).
- Assuming this endpoint returns every kind of sign-in. The v1.0 documentation says interactive sign-ins and successful federated sign-ins are included; non-interactive, service principal and managed identity sign-ins are reported separately in the portal and are not covered by these requests.
- Relying on a filter property that the documentation does not list. Only createdDateTime and appDisplayName are shown in the official examples; filters such as userPrincipalName, status/errorCode, conditionalAccessStatus and isInteractive are widely used but you should test them in Graph Explorer, and compare the result with the portal because unsupported query parameters can fail silently.

## Performance and throttling notes
$top is limited to 1000. Large exports are better done in daily windows than in one huge request. The sign-in endpoint has its own throttling limits; respect Retry-After on 429 responses and use exponential back-off. For continuous analysis, stream the logs to Log Analytics or a storage account with diagnostic settings instead of polling the API.

title: Track user changes with the Microsoft Graph users delta query and paging
summary: How to run the initial users delta sync, follow nextLink and deltaLink, and process changes and deletions on later runs without re-reading the directory.
body:
## What it does
Delta query returns only what changed since your last call, which is ideal for keeping an HR system, a database or a search index in sync with Microsoft Entra ID. The first run enumerates all users; later runs return created, updated and deleted users only.

## Step 1: initial synchronisation
Send a delta request with all query parameters you need. Other parameters can only be set on this first request; Graph encodes them into the tokens.
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$select=displayName,userPrincipalName,accountEnabled,department,jobTitle
Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=200
```

The response contains a page of users and an @odata.nextLink:
```json
{
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$skiptoken=[skiptoken]",
  "value": [ { "id": "[object-id]", "displayName": "Anna Meyer", "userPrincipalName": "anna@contoso.example" } ]
}
```

## Step 2: follow the pages
Call the complete @odata.nextLink URL unchanged until the response contains @odata.deltaLink instead.
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$skiptoken=[skiptoken]
```
The last page returns:
```json
{
  "@odata.deltaLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$deltatoken=[deltatoken]",
  "value": []
}
```
Store the deltaLink securely (it is a pointer into tenant data) and discard the nextLinks.

## Step 3: incremental runs
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$deltatoken=[deltatoken]
```
Handle each item in value:
- A normal object with changed properties: create or update the record by id.
- An object containing "@removed": {"reason": "deleted"}: delete or deactivate the record.
Then continue until the new @odata.deltaLink appears and store it, replacing the old one.

## Only changed properties
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$deltatoken=[deltatoken]
Prefer: return=minimal
```
With return=minimal the response contains only the properties that changed. A property set to null is still included, so you can detect clearing a value.

## Track specific users only
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$filter=id eq '[object-id-1]' or id eq '[object-id-2]'
```
The only supported filter on this endpoint is on id, with a maximum of 50 objects.

## How to adapt
- Groups, applications, directory roles and many other directory resources have delta functions with the same pattern (for example /groups/delta).
- Store the deltaLink per sync job; running two consumers against one stored link causes missed changes.
- Schedule the job every 5 to 30 minutes; there is no value in polling faster than your data changes.

## Required permissions
Delegated: User.Read.All (higher privileged options include Directory.Read.All). Application: User.Read.All. Personal Microsoft accounts are not supported. Reading sensitive properties may require additional permissions.

## Common mistakes
- Changing $select between runs: query parameters live in the token; start a new sync instead.
- Keeping the nextLink as the checkpoint: only the deltaLink is the checkpoint.
- Not handling @removed objects, so deleted accounts stay in the target system.
- Expecting licenseAssignmentStates changes to appear; they are not tracked by user delta.
- Assuming the order of changes: use the last occurrence of an id if it appears twice.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use the Prefer: odata.maxpagesize header to control page size, and a narrow $select to keep responses small. If a deltaLink expires (the service returns an error such as 410 Gone, or a sync state not found message) start again with a full enumeration and reconcile. On HTTP 429 wait for Retry-After before the next page.

title: Microsoft 365 groups in Graph: inventory with owners, ownerless groups and transitive members
summary: Requests to list Microsoft 365 and Teams-enabled groups, expand owners, find groups without owners or members, and read nested membership.
body:
## What it does
Group sprawl is a governance problem: groups without owners, empty groups, and groups whose membership is hidden in nested groups. These requests inventory groups and answer these questions. Note that advanced queries cannot be combined with $expand, so owners are retrieved in one request and ownerless groups in another.

## Requests

Microsoft 365 groups with creation date and owners:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'Unified')&$select=id,displayName,mail,visibility,createdDateTime,resourceProvisioningOptions&$expand=owners($select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName)&$top=100
```

Groups that are Teams-enabled:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=resourceProvisioningOptions/Any(x:x eq 'Team')&$select=id,displayName,visibility
```

Groups without owners (advanced query, no $expand):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=owners/$count eq 0&$count=true&$select=id,displayName,createdDateTime
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Groups without members:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=members/$count eq 0&$count=true&$select=id,displayName,createdDateTime
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Dynamic membership groups:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'DynamicMembership')&$select=id,displayName,membershipRule,membershipRuleProcessingState
```

Direct members (users only) with count:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/[group-id]/members/microsoft.graph.user?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName&$count=true&$top=100
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Members including nested groups (transitive):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/[group-id]/transitiveMembers/microsoft.graph.user?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Owners of one group:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/[group-id]/owners?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName
```

## How to adapt
- Stale groups: combine the inventory with the Microsoft 365 group activity report (/reports/getOffice365GroupsActivityDetail(period='D90')) to find groups with no recent activity.
- Fix an ownerless group: POST /groups/[group-id]/owners/$ref with body {"@odata.id": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/[user-id]"}.
- Security groups only: $filter=securityEnabled eq true and mailEnabled eq false.

## Required permissions
- Reading groups, owners and members: delegated Group.Read.All or GroupMember.Read.All (for membership only); application Group.Read.All or GroupMember.Read.All. Directory.Read.All also works but is broader.
- Adding an owner: Group.ReadWrite.All (or Directory.ReadWrite.All), and an appropriate role such as Groups Administrator for delegated calls.
- Reports: Reports.Read.All.

## Common mistakes
- Adding $expand to an advanced query: it is not supported; use a second request.
- $expand=owners returns at most 20 items per group; query /owners if you need all.
- Forgetting the type cast microsoft.graph.user and getting groups and devices mixed in the members list.
- Missing ConsistencyLevel header or $count=true on count-based filters.
- Assuming members includes nested members; use transitiveMembers for that.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select, as groups have many properties. Expanding owners for 5,000 groups is cheaper than one call per group, but on large tenants use $top=100 or less with $expand. Directory throttling is per tenant; honour Retry-After. For regular inventories, run it weekly and store the result, rather than querying live every time.

title: SharePoint via Microsoft Graph: find a site, list its lists and filter list items on fields
summary: Requests to resolve a site by path, enumerate lists and libraries, and query list items with $expand=fields and $filter, including the indexed column caveat.
body:
## What it does
This sequence takes you from a SharePoint URL to the items in a list: resolve the site id, list the lists and document libraries, then read items with selected fields and a filter. It replaces many CSOM or REST scripts with plain Graph calls.

## Step 1: get the site
By path (hostname, colon, server-relative path):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/contoso.sharepoint.com:/sites/Marketing?$select=id,displayName,webUrl
```
By keyword search:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites?search=marketing&$select=id,displayName,webUrl
```
The id has the form hostname,site-collection-guid,web-guid. Use the complete value in later URLs.

## Step 2: lists and libraries
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists?$select=id,displayName,webUrl,list&$top=100
```
The list facet shows the template (for example genericList or documentLibrary) and whether the list is hidden. Document libraries also appear as drives:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/drives?$select=id,name,driveType,webUrl
```

## Step 3: columns
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/columns?$select=name,displayName,indexed,readOnly
```
Use the internal name (name) in $select and $filter, not the display name.

## Step 4: items with fields and a filter
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items?$expand=fields($select=Title,Status,DueDate)&$filter=fields/Status eq 'Open'&$top=200
Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly
```
The Prefer header allows filtering on a column that is not indexed. Without it, Graph returns an error asking you to index the column. The header is described in Microsoft Q&A and community answers rather than on the listItem reference page, and its name is a warning: such queries can fail on large lists (over the list view threshold of 5,000 items), so index the column instead whenever you can.

Response:
```json
{
  "value": [
    { "id": "12", "webUrl": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Marketing/Lists/Tasks/12_.000",
      "fields": { "Title": "Prepare campaign", "Status": "Open", "DueDate": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" } }
  ],
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items?$skiptoken=[token]"
}
```

## Create an item
```http
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items
Content-Type: application/json

{ "fields": { "Title": "New task", "Status": "Open" } }
```

## How to adapt
- Users in person columns appear as lookup ids (AuthorLookupId); resolve them separately.
- Filter by date: $filter=fields/DueDate lt '2026-12-31T00:00:00Z' on an indexed column.
- Change tracking: GET /sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items/delta for incremental reads.

## Required permissions
- Read sites, lists and items: delegated Sites.Read.All; application Sites.Read.All.
- Create or update items: Sites.ReadWrite.All.
- For application access limited to chosen sites, use Sites.Selected and grant the app per site through the site permissions endpoint; this is the recommended least privilege for production apps.

## Common mistakes
- Using the display name of a column instead of its internal name (for example Due_x0020_Date).
- Filtering on several indexed columns at once; only one indexed field can be filtered at a time.
- Forgetting $expand=fields: items then only contain metadata, not your column values.
- Truncating the site id; use the whole three-part value.
- Granting Sites.Read.All to an automation that only needs one site.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select inside fields to cut payload. Page with @odata.nextLink; $top up to 200 is typical for list items. SharePoint throttles by resource units and returns 429 or 503 with Retry-After; always honour it, and send a descriptive User-Agent for app traffic as recommended in the SharePoint throttling guidance.

title: OneDrive and SharePoint library change tracking with drive delta and downloadUrl
summary: Use the drive delta function for an initial sync and incremental changes, handle deleted items, and download file content without extra permission lookups.
body:
## What it does
Delta query on a drive returns files and folders that were added, changed or deleted since your last call. It is the right tool for backup jobs, search indexers and compliance exports that must not rescan millions of files every night. It works for OneDrive and for SharePoint document libraries.

## Choose the drive
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/drive?$select=id,driveType,webUrl
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/drives?$select=id,name,webUrl
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/[user-id]/drive?$select=id,webUrl
```

## Initial enumeration
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?$select=id,name,size,lastModifiedDateTime,file,folder,deleted,parentReference&$top=200
```
Follow @odata.nextLink until the response contains @odata.deltaLink. Store the deltaLink.

```json
{
  "value": [
    { "id": "[item-id]", "name": "Budget.xlsx", "size": 48213, "lastModifiedDateTime": "2026-11-18T09:12:44Z",
      "file": { "mimeType": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet" },
      "parentReference": { "driveId": "[drive-id]", "id": "[parent-id]" } },
    { "id": "[other-item-id]", "name": "old.txt", "deleted": {} }
  ],
  "@odata.deltaLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?token=[token]"
}
```

## Incremental run
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?token=[token]
```
Apply each item by id. Items with the deleted facet must be removed from your index. The same item can appear more than once; use the last occurrence. parentReference.path is not populated in delta results, so track the hierarchy by ids.

## Start from now (skip history)
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?token=latest
```
This returns an empty value array and a deltaLink for future changes.

## Download content
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/items/[item-id]/content
```
The response is a redirect (302) to a short-lived pre-authenticated URL. Alternatively request it in the metadata: $select=id,name,@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl. Do not store download URLs; they expire after a short time and must not be shared.

## Resync handling
If the service cannot return changes for your token, it responds with 410 Gone and a Location header for a fresh enumeration. After the enumeration, reconcile with your local state (the error code resyncChangesApplyDifferences or resyncChangesUploadDifferences tells you how).

## How to adapt
- Sharing changes: add the headers Prefer: deltashowremovedasdeleted, deltatraversepermissiongaps, deltashowsharingchanges to get sharing-change annotations; permission scanning scenarios require the Sites.FullControl.All application permission.
- A single folder is not a documented delta scope; run delta on the root and filter by parent ids on your side.
- Large files: a simple upload (PUT .../content) supports files up to 250 MB; above that, or for resumable uploads, use createUploadSession.

## Required permissions
Delegated: Files.Read (least privileged for own drive), Files.Read.All for other drives; Sites.Read.All also works for SharePoint libraries. Application: Files.Read.All (or Sites.Read.All). Application access to all files is highly sensitive; prefer Sites.Selected where the scenario allows it.

## Common mistakes
- Trying to rebuild paths from parentReference.path in delta results.
- Treating deltaLink as permanent: protect it like a credential, and handle 410.
- Deleting a folder locally before its children are processed; delete folders only when empty.
- Logging download URLs.
- Starting a new full enumeration every night instead of using the stored deltaLink.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select to avoid large payloads and $top for page size. SharePoint and OneDrive throttle by resource units; delta calls are cheaper than recursive children listing. On 429 or 503, respect Retry-After, and schedule heavy initial enumerations outside business hours.

title: Mailbox triage with Microsoft Graph: unread filter, $select, move and mark as read
summary: Requests for reading unread inbox messages efficiently, searching, moving messages to folders, marking them read, and tracking changes with message delta.
body:
## What it does
Build a lightweight triage tool or automation: list unread messages from the last day, pull only the fields you need, move processed messages to a folder, and track new arrivals with delta. All requests use the signed-in mailbox (/me) and can be switched to /users/[id] for application access.

## Requests

Unread messages from a given time, newest first (properties in $orderby must also appear in $filter):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/mailFolders/inbox/messages?$filter=isRead eq false and receivedDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$orderby=receivedDateTime desc&$select=id,subject,from,receivedDateTime,hasAttachments,importance,webLink&$top=25
```

Text body instead of HTML (smaller, easier to process):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages/[message-id]?$select=subject,body,from
Prefer: outlook.body-content-type="text"
```

Search (cannot be combined with $filter or $orderby):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$search="from:anna AND subject:budget"&$select=id,subject,from,receivedDateTime&$top=25
```

Messages with attachments from a sender:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$filter=from/emailAddress/address eq 'anna@contoso.example' and hasAttachments eq true&$select=id,subject,receivedDateTime
```

List folders to get the target folder id:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/mailFolders?$select=id,displayName,totalItemCount,unreadItemCount&$top=50
```

Mark as read:
```http
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages/[message-id]
Content-Type: application/json

{ "isRead": true }
```

Move to a folder (a well-known name such as archive also works as destinationId):
```http
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages/[message-id]/move
Content-Type: application/json

{ "destinationId": "[folder-id]" }
```
The move returns a new message with a new id, so store the returned id if you need to reference it later.

Incremental changes in the inbox:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/mailFolders/inbox/messages/delta?$select=subject,from,receivedDateTime,isRead
Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=50
```
Follow @odata.nextLink until @odata.deltaLink, store it, and call it on the next run.

## How to adapt
- Application access to a shared mailbox: replace /me with /users/[mailbox-id-or-upn] and limit the app with an application access policy in Exchange Online, so it cannot read every mailbox.
- Stable ids across moves: add Prefer: IdType="ImmutableId".
- Categorise instead of move: PATCH with {"categories": ["Processed"]}.

## Required permissions
- Read: delegated Mail.Read (Mail.ReadBasic for limited fields); application Mail.Read.
- Mark as read, move, categorise: Mail.ReadWrite.
- Send mail would need Mail.Send; keep triage tools read/write only.
- Application permissions grant access to all mailboxes unless restricted by an application access policy or role-based access control for applications in Exchange Online.

## Common mistakes
- Combining $search with $filter or $orderby: not supported.
- Ordering by a property that is not in the filter: the request fails with an InefficientFilter error.
- Reading full HTML bodies for thousands of messages when only metadata is needed.
- Reusing the original id after a move.
- Granting tenant-wide Mail.ReadWrite to a simple automation.

## Performance and throttling notes
Outlook resources allow a limited number of concurrent requests per app and mailbox (commonly four), and 429 responses carry Retry-After. Use $select, $top up to 50 for bodies and larger for metadata, and delta instead of repeated full scans. Batch several reads with $batch, but keep concurrency modest.

title: Security alerts_v2 and incidents in Microsoft Graph: filter, triage and update alerts
summary: Requests to list alerts by severity, status and source, read incidents with alerts, and update status, classification and assignment of an alert.
body:
## What it does
The unified Microsoft Graph security API exposes alerts and incidents from Microsoft Defender XDR products and other sources in one place. These requests let a script or SOC dashboard pull high-severity new alerts, see them grouped as incidents, and update their state. Use alerts_v2 and incidents; the older legacy alerts endpoint is deprecated.

## Requests

New high-severity alerts (alerts_v2 documents $filter, $top, $skip and $count; it does not document $orderby, and recent alerts are returned first):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=severity eq 'high' and status eq 'new'&$top=100
```

Alerts from one product created after a date:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=serviceSource eq 'microsoftDefenderForEndpoint' and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=100
```

Alerts assigned to an analyst:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=assignedTo eq 'analyst@contoso.example'
```

One alert with its details and evidence:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2/[alert-id]
```

Active incidents with their alerts:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/incidents?$filter=status eq 'active'&$expand=alerts&$top=25
```

## Update an alert
```http
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2/[alert-id]
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "status": "inProgress",
  "assignedTo": "analyst@contoso.example",
  "classification": "truePositive",
  "determination": "malware"
}
```
Valid status values are new, inProgress and resolved. Classification and determination use the enumerations documented for the alert resource (for example falsePositive, truePositive, informationalExpectedActivity). Set them when resolving an alert.

## Paging
Responses contain @odata.nextLink while more alerts remain. Follow it. You can also page with $top and $skip as in $top=100&$skip=200, but nextLink is more robust.

## How to adapt
- Daily digest: filter on createdDateTime for the last 24 hours and group by serviceSource and severity on the client.
- Only unresolved: status ne 'resolved' (check the filter support for ne on the property in the current documentation).
- Hand off to a ticket system: store alert id, incidentId, title, severity, and the alertWebUrl property so analysts can open the Defender portal directly.

## Required permissions
- Read alerts: SecurityAlert.Read.All (delegated and application).
- Update alerts: SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All.
- Read incidents: SecurityIncident.Read.All; update incidents: SecurityIncident.ReadWrite.All.
- Delegated calls also need the signed-in user to hold a supported role, for example Security Reader, Global Reader, Security Operator or Security Administrator.

## Common mistakes
- Calling the deprecated /security/alerts endpoint in new code.
- Using $orderby or $expand=evidence on alerts_v2 and getting errors; they are not documented for that endpoint.
- Using filter properties that are not supported; filters work on assignedTo, classification, determination, createdDateTime, lastUpdateDateTime, severity, serviceSource and status.
- Forgetting that application permissions here expose all security data in the tenant; protect the app registration, use certificates, and restrict who can use it.
- Updating status without a classification when resolving.

## Performance and throttling notes
Security API calls are throttled per app and tenant; keep polling at a sensible interval (every few minutes is usually enough) and honour Retry-After. Prefer filters on createdDateTime or lastUpdateDateTime so each poll fetches only recent alerts, and store the timestamp of the last processed alert as your checkpoint.

title: Intune managed devices in Graph: find noncompliant Windows devices and trigger a sync
summary: Requests to list managed devices with $filter and $select, look at compliance and last sync time, and send a sync action to selected devices.
body:
## What it does
Use these requests to get a current view of device compliance without opening the Intune admin center: noncompliant Windows devices, devices that have not checked in for a while, and the details of one device. Then trigger a remote sync for a device so that it reports compliance again. Intune license is required in the tenant.

## Requests

Test first: the Microsoft Learn page for listing managedDevices shows no $filter examples and does not say which properties and operators are supported. The three filter requests below use properties that exist on the managedDevice resource (complianceState, operatingSystem, lastSyncDateTime, userPrincipalName), but filter support per property is not documented. Run each one in Graph Explorer first and compare the count with the Intune admin center, because unsupported query parameters can fail silently. If a filter misbehaves, drop it and filter on the client side after $select.

Noncompliant Windows devices (test first; complianceState values are lowercase: compliant, noncompliant, inGracePeriod, conflict, error, unknown, configManager):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$filter=complianceState eq 'noncompliant' and operatingSystem eq 'Windows'&$select=id,deviceName,userPrincipalName,operatingSystem,osVersion,complianceState,lastSyncDateTime,managedDeviceOwnerType&$top=100
```

Devices that last synced before a date (test first):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$filter=lastSyncDateTime le 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z&$select=id,deviceName,userPrincipalName,lastSyncDateTime,complianceState&$top=100
```

Devices of one user (test first):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$filter=userPrincipalName eq 'anna@contoso.example'&$select=id,deviceName,operatingSystem,complianceState
```

One device with full details:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices/[managed-device-id]
```

Compliance policy results for one device:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices/[managed-device-id]/deviceCompliancePolicyStates
```

Trigger a sync (no request body, returns 204 No Content):
```http
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices/[managed-device-id]/syncDevice
```

## Response example
```json
{
  "value": [
    {
      "id": "[managed-device-id]",
      "deviceName": "LT-ANNA-01",
      "userPrincipalName": "anna@contoso.example",
      "operatingSystem": "Windows",
      "osVersion": "10.0.26100.1000",
      "complianceState": "noncompliant",
      "lastSyncDateTime": "2026-11-18T07:41:09Z"
    }
  ],
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$skiptoken=[token]"
}
```

## How to adapt
- Not every property supports every operator in Intune endpoints. If a filter returns an error, test it in Graph Explorer, filter by another property, or filter on the client side after $select.
- Join to Microsoft Entra ID with the azureADDeviceId property to find the directory device object.
- Report on all platforms by dropping the operatingSystem filter, or use iOS, Android and macOS values.
- Devices in a grace period report inGracePeriod, not noncompliant, so the first request does not return them; query complianceState eq 'inGracePeriod' separately if you need them.
- Bulk sync: loop over the ids returned by the first request, with a delay between calls and the $batch endpoint (up to 20 sync requests per batch).

## Required permissions
- Reading managed devices: DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All (delegated and application).
- Sync and other remote actions: DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All (delegated and application). Do not use ReadWrite permissions for actions that require this one.
- Delegated calls also require an Intune role with the corresponding rights, for example Help Desk Operator or Intune Administrator through role-based access control.

## Common mistakes
- Trusting an undocumented $filter without testing it; managedDevices filters are not covered by the reference page.
- Sending a body with syncDevice; the request body must be empty.
- Using the Microsoft Entra device id instead of the Intune managed device id in the URL.
- Granting PrivilegedOperations.All to a reporting app that only needs Read.All.
- Treating lastSyncDateTime as the last user activity; it is the last check-in with Intune.
- Ignoring paging and only seeing the first 100 devices.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select to avoid the large default device object. Intune applies service-specific throttling; on 429 respond to Retry-After and keep sync loops slow (for example one call per second). Remote actions are queued, and the device syncs when it next contacts the service, so do not retry repeatedly. For very large estates, use Intune data exports or the reporting endpoints under /deviceManagement/reports for bulk data, rather than paging through every device.
